editorial:
S. Marshal, but in reality, you are a bank robber on the run. That is exactly what happens to Joe Maybe. He gets caught in a wild lie that lands him in a small town where he has to act like a hero. Things get even crazier when his ex-girlfriend shows up, and the two of them have to pretend to be a loving married couple to keep the secret. Along the way, they bond with a sweet orphan boy, and you can really feel Joe starting to wish his fake life was actually real.

What makes this flick work is the great chemistry between the leads and the constant tension of Joe getting caught. The pacing stays brisk, though some of the romance feels a bit old-fashioned. If you like Westerns with a bit of a comedy twist and some heart, you will love this. It is a cozy, fun ride that keeps you guessing.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when Joe's old gang arrives to rob the town bank. Instead of joining his old friends, Joe chooses to protect the town and the people he has come to love. He leads the fight against the criminals in a big showdown. After the bad guys are defeated, Joe is forgiven for his past mistakes. He finally stops pretending and gets to live a real, honest life with his partner and the boy.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old school Westerns with a romantic twist.
